CONFIRM C0004 | `scan_health()` sets `tools_available[tool_name] = True` whenever a runner returns normally, but each runner returns `[]` on `_run_tool(...)->stderr=="NOT_FOUND"`. Missing binaries therefore report as available with zero diagnostics, which misleads the insect brain’s health signal.

CONFIRM C0005 | `endocrine.py` advertises CrossHair in the module docstring, defines `CROSSHAIR_BIN` and `_CROSSHAIR_TIMEOUT`, but never invokes it in `scan_health()` or elsewhere. The documented health-scan feature is partially dead and can never fire.

CONFIRM C0007 | `health_trend()` appends counts only for categories present in each scan: categories absent in a round contribute no zero entry, so series lengths diverge and per-round alignment is lost.

CONFIRM C0003 | `compute_pacing_signals()` computes median with `sorted(vals)[len(vals)//2]`, which is the upper middle element for even-length lists rather than the statistical median. That biases slow-model and response-size anomaly thresholds.

EXTEND C0009 | The mislabeled response-size anomaly is not just nomenclature. It collapses two distinct causes into the same `signal_type="context_growth"`, so any downstream consumer that buckets by `signal_type` cannot distinguish total accumulated-context pressure from a single model’s oversized output. That can produce the wrong mitigation path when the insect brain reacts to pacing signals.

CONFIRM C0017 | Interface risk is real. `EndocrineLayer.run()`/`compute_pacing_signals()` require `RoundTiming` objects with attribute access (`rt.duration_s`, `rt.response_chars`, `rt.model_id`), while the surrounding bench code commonly passes plain dict-like JSON-shaped structures between layers. Without normalization, this path fails at runtime when endocrine is wired to persisted or orchestrator-produced timing records.

FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.96
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.62
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` does not actually run tests against the patched code. It writes only the target file’s basename into a tempdir (`patched_path = tmpdir / basename(target_path)`), but then executes the provided `test_cmd` unchanged. In the active immune pipeline call site, that command is `["python3", "-m", "pytest", "bench/tests/", ...]`, which resolves tests from the real repository under `cwd=tmpdir`. The patched file is not placed at its original package path (e.g. `bench/endocrine.py`), no full source tree is copied, and `PYTHONPATH` is not redirected. Result: imports during pytest still resolve to the original source tree, so fix evaluation can report SAFE/NEUTRAL/HARMFUL based on tests that never exercised the patched code.
FOLLOW: This breaks the endocrine layer’s key new capability: sandbox fix verification. Downstream, immune Stage 4 marks findings `verified=True` when evaluation returns SAFE/NEUTRAL. Because tests are running against unmodified source, harmful fixes can be falsely verified and trigger the NK “bug closed” gate in later rounds, suppressing rediscovery of still-open bugs. The defect crosses the endocrine→immune interface and directly corrupts canonical finding lifecycle state, not just reporting.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — create the patched file inside the tempdir under its original relative path from the repo root (e.g. `tmpdir/bench/endocrine.py`), copy the rest of the source tree needed for imports/tests into that tempdir, and run `test_cmd` there so pytest imports the sandboxed tree instead of the live source.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.93
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: FIND — post-fix static analysis in `evaluate_fix()` is performed on the isolated patched file only, not in project context. `run_pyright([patched_path])`, `run_ruff([patched_path])`, and `run_bandit([patched_path])` analyze a temp file whose path no longer matches the package layout and whose sibling modules are absent. For endocrine-layer fixes that change imports, types, or interfaces, this can miss project-integration breakage entirely or produce different diagnostics than the real tree. Evidence: only `os.path.basename(target_path)` is written into tempdir; no containing package structure or dependent modules are present.
FOLLOW: The verdict logic uses only delta counts from these isolated tool runs plus optional tests. Because both pre- and post-fix scans are context-mismatched, a fix that breaks imports or type relations against `immune_agents.py` / `insect_brain.py` can still be labeled SAFE/NEUTRAL. That again feeds immune Stage 4 verification and can incorrectly mark a proposed fix as verified, closing bugs that are actually unresolved in the integrated bench.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — evaluate pre/post tool diagnostics against a sandbox copy of the relevant project tree preserving original paths, then run pyright/ruff/bandit from that sandbox root on the sandboxed file path (or project root if needed) so diagnostics reflect the actual package/import context.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.88
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.47
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` can classify a fix as `SAFE` even when it leaves the target bug unchanged. The function labels any case with `total_net == 0` and `tests_passed is True` as SAFE, and any case with `total_net < 0` as SAFE even if the reduction is from unrelated warnings. There is no check that the original finding’s referenced diagnostic disappeared or that the specific defect improved. This is especially visible because `evaluate_fix()` compares only aggregate counts, not finding-specific before/after evidence.
FOLLOW: Endocrine fix evaluation is then used by the immune pipeline to set `finding.verified=True` for SAFE or NEUTRAL results. A no-op or irrelevant edit can therefore verify and close a bug as long as tests pass or aggregate counts do not worsen. Downstream this poisons dedup/closure behavior and misleads human review with a false “programmatically verified” status.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — require at least one root-cause improvement before returning SAFE: either a strict decrease in diagnostics on the target file or successful tests plus a non-zero beneficial delta. If there is zero net change, return NEUTRAL even when tests pass.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.78
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.39
DESCRIPTION: FIND — the “defect detection” feature described in the module docstring is not implemented as a standalone function or API. The file only categorizes tool diagnostics opportunistically inside runner helpers (`_categorise_pyright`, `_categorise_ruff`) and has no exported defect-detection pass matching the stated capability “Defect detection — classify findings by defect category.” There is also no use of `DefectCategory.OFF_BY_ONE`, `RACE_CONDITION`, or `UNKNOWN` in any actual detection pipeline.
FOLLOW: This leaves a declared endocrine feature partially dead: reviewers and the insect brain can only consume raw tool-derived categories, not a coherent defect-classification stage over findings. Downstream expectations about category coverage are unmet, and several declared categories can never fire, reducing usefulness of health metrics and making parts of the interface misleading.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — either remove the standalone “Defect detection” capability claim and unused categories for PoC, or add a minimal exported classifier function that maps `ToolDiagnostic` objects into the declared category set and is called from `scan_health()`. For PoC simplicity, remove the unsupported claim/categories that never fire.
VERIFIED: TRUE
